There was a caste system, and it had a design: keep the lowest class uneducated, keep them marrying within the same class, and the system renews itself for free.

Kevin isn't offering an opinion here - this is the actual history of how the Vedic caste system in India worked, and how the people running it talked about it. No schooling. No reading. No writing. Just enough to milk the cows and stay exactly where you were born.

The uncomfortable part isn't the history. It's recognizing the same shape, still running, somewhere in your own life.

The merchants made the money. The warriors made the rules.

Warriors weren't the smartest class in the old caste system - they were the biggest and strongest, and that's what let them run the wars. They'd walk up to a peasant, hand him a spear, and say you're coming with us. No choice in it. Many came back without an arm, and went right back to the fields.

Here's the part almost nobody says out loud: being strong enough to force people into war is how the warrior class became royalty. Not wisdom. Force, repeated long enough that everyone forgot to question it.
